messages:
maria: seeing p99 jump to ~1.8s in us-east-1 hosted API around 17:08 UTC, only on text.generate route. queue depth spiked from ~20 -> ~400. looks like a single tenant flooded with short requests.

alex: rolling up... any correlation with the kernel-selector change we shipped yesterday?

maria: kernel-selector v3.2 rolled to us-east canary at 16:45, went prod at 16:55. metrics looked fine for 10m, spike starts 17:06.

kevin: grabbing logs now. preliminary: tons of short requests (seq_len=16) causing batches of ~512 which triggers KV cache churn and evictions. sample log: 
```json
{"req_id":"r-abc123","tenant":"tenant-8812","seq_len":16,"batch_size":512,"kvcache_hits":0,"kvcache_evictions":12}
```

jen: hmm the batcher should cap batch sizes for short sequences. I did push a `batch_timeout_ms` tweak to stage yesterday that favors bigger batches for throughput. did that go to prod too?

alex: i reverted it in stage but forgot to block prod rollout.

maria: tenant id looks like `tenant-8812` — QPS for that tenant jumped 7x. could be a client bug or loadtest.

opsbot: alert: tenant-8812 QPS 7200 for text.generate, aux-kernel fallback in 13% of requests.

kevin: kernel-selector logs show many fallbacks to aux kernel which has higher per-call overhead -> ~2x latency when fallback happens. reason: kernel scoring favored a kernel optimized for long sequences after the scoring weight change.

jen: immediate mitigations: 1) apply per-tenant soft rate cap 2) lower max_batch for seq_len < 32 3) pin tenant to aux-optimized kernel or vice-versa depending on profiling.

alex: applying rate cap now through rateengine: `rateengine apply tenant-8812 --rps 1000`

maria: rate cap applied. seeing queue depth fall, p95 down to ~420ms, p99 ~900ms and dropping.

kevin: spinning a perf profile on an affected host, uploading flamegraph: https://s3.internal/redwood/fg/3498765432.svg

jen: early hypothesis: kernel scoring weights changed to prefer throughput created a mismatch for tiny-request patterns. that kernel forces large coalesced batches which overwhelms KV cache and causes eviction storms. batcher hysteresis then amplifies.

alex: agreed. action items: (A) rollback kernel-scoring weight change in prod (B) implement sequence-length-aware max_batch (C) add eviction backpressure -> throttle.

maria: i'm opening PRs for (B) and (C) now and will coordinate the rollback for (A). will also draft an incident note.

deploy-bot: rollback started: kernel-selector config -> v3.1 at 18:05 UTC.

maria: p99 recovered to ~210ms after rollback. system stabilizing, marking incident mitigated.

kevin: adding long-term metric request: `kvcache_eviction_rate` per-tenant and an alert threshold.

jen: +1, and please add a canary gate that runs a short-seq synthetic workload for any kernel scoring change. avoids regressions like this.

maria: thanks everyone. I'll draft the postmortem and tag infra/ops and eng-runtime follow-ups. :thumbsup:
